About: Rolling Without Slipping — Shape Sets the Split

Source

Topic
Rigid-body rotation & rolling motion (JEE / NCERT Class 11)
Concept
For rolling without slipping, the energy split between translation and rotation is fixed by the body's shape alone — independent of mass, radius and speed.
Serves
Constraint ω = v/r · KE = ½mv² + ½Iω² · shape coefficient c = I/(mr²) · misconception "the contact point moves fastest"
Inquiry
Hoop vs solid sphere at the same speed: which spends more of its energy spinning?
Misconception
"The rim meets the road, so the contact point is moving fastest." It is instantaneously AT REST.

Guided Inquiry

1 · Watch the rim

A solid disc is rolling to the right. A single point on its rim traces the pink curve — a cycloid. Watch it sweep forward fastest over the top and pause at the bottom, each time it touches the ground.

Next you will predict which point on the wheel is moving fastest at a given instant — then the velocity arrows will label the contact, centre and top.

2 · Predict — which point moves fastest?

The wheel is rolling without slipping. Which point on the rim has the greatest speed at this instant?

3 · Predict — hoop vs solid sphere

A hoop and a solid sphere roll along at the same speed v. Which one has more of its kinetic energy tied up in spinning?

4 · Verify with the star control

Use the shape picker in the Controls panel: switch between hoop and solid sphere and watch the stacked bar.

The hoop sits at 1/2. The sphere at 2/7 ≈ 0.286. The ratio comes from c = I/(mr²) alone.

5 · Now break it — try to move the split

Pick any shape. Drag mass from 0.5 to 5 kg. Drag speed from 1 to 8 m/s. The energy bar changes size — the total KE grows and shrinks — but the rotational fraction refuses to move.

That's the whole point: the split is c/(1+c), and c is a pure number that depends only on how the mass is distributed. Not on how much mass, not on how big the wheel, not on how fast it rolls.

The Physics

Rolling Without Slipping — Shape Sets the Split · what this sim shows, the physics behind it, and every control

01

At a glance

A wheel rolls along the ground without sliding. A pink dot on its rim leaves a looping trace, and the kinetic energy of the wheel is shown in two parts, one for moving forward and one for spinning.

What you'll learn

  • How the spin rate of a rolling wheel is tied to its forward speed.
  • How the speed of a point on the rim depends on where it is on the wheel.
  • How the shape of the body enters its kinetic energy.
The wheel on level ground, the pink rim dot and the trace it leaves.

What's on screen

  • Wheel (teal outline) with a cross that shows how it turns. A line above gives the shape and its c.
  • Rim dot and trace (pink): the path of one point on the rim.
  • Blue arrows with labels: the speed at three points of the wheel.
  • Energy bar (bottom right): a teal part for moving forward and a pink part for spinning, with the energy in joules.
See itStart with the solid disc at the default settings. Watch for: the pink dot drawing a looping curve as the wheel rolls.

Fixed: the wheel rolls on level ground at a constant speed without sliding. The body is uniform, so its mass spreads evenly around the shape.

03

Rolling without slipping ties the spin rate to the speed: ω = v/r

If the wheel does not slide, each turn lays one rim length 2πr along the ground. In one turn the centre advances 2πr, so its speed v and the spin rate ω are linked:

v = ω r, so ω = v / r
v in m/s, r in m, ω in rad/s.

A smaller wheel must spin faster to keep the same speed. The sim reads ω from this rule, and the pink dot traces a curve called a cycloid.

vrω = v/r
4.0 m/s0.30 m13.33 rad/s
8.0 m/s0.15 m53.33 rad/s
1.0 m/s0.60 m1.67 rad/s
See itTake the smallest wheel at the top speed, r = 0.15 m and v = 8.0 m/s. Watch for: the ω readout at 53.33 rad/s.
04

The top of the wheel moves at 2v while the contact point is at rest

Each rim point has two motions: the forward speed v of the whole wheel, plus a spin speed ωr = v along the rim. Where the two point the same way they add, and where they point opposite ways they cancel:

PointForwardSpinTotal at v = 4.0 m/s
Topv →v →2v = 8.0 m/s
Centrev →nonev = 4.0 m/s
Contactv →v ←0

The contact point is at rest only for an instant. A new rim point touches the ground every moment, so the wheel as a whole keeps moving. This zero speed is why no rubbing happens at the ground.

See itKeep the default v = 4.0 m/s and read the blue labels. Watch for: 2v = 8.0 m/s at the top, v = 4.0 m/s at the centre and 0 at the contact.
05

Kinetic energy adds as ½mv² + ½Iω², so the spinning share is c/(1 + c)

A rolling body moves forward and spins at once, so its two energies add. For a uniform shape I = c m r², and ω = v/r turns the spin part into ½ c m v²:

KE = ½ m v² + ½ I ω² = ½ m v² (1 + c)
KErot / KE = c / (1 + c)

The shape enters only through c. Mass far from the centre gives a larger c, so a hoop spends more of its energy on spinning than a solid sphere does. With m = 2.0 kg, r = 0.30 m and v = 4.0 m/s, the forward part is 16.0 J for every shape:

Shapecc/(1+c)KErot
Thin hoop10.50016.0 J
Hollow sphere2/30.40010.7 J
Solid disc1/20.3338.0 J
Solid sphere2/50.2866.4 J
See itPick the thin hoop. Watch for: the rotational fraction 0.500, with equal teal and pink parts of 16.0 J.
See itNow pick the solid sphere. Watch for: the rotational fraction 0.286, with a pink part of 6.4 J.
06

Mass, radius and speed leave the split unchanged

The fraction c/(1 + c) contains only c, and c depends only on how the mass is spread through the shape. In KErot = ½ c m v², the mass m and the speed v scale both parts of the energy together. The radius cancels once ω = v/r is used.

So a heavier, bigger or faster wheel carries more total energy, but the same share of it is spinning:

Solid discKEtransKErotFraction
m 2.0, r 0.30, v 4.016.0 J8.0 J0.333
m 5.0, r 0.15, v 8.0160.0 J80.0 J0.333
m 5.0, r 0.60, v 8.0160.0 J80.0 J0.333
See itSet the disc to m = 5.0 kg, r = 0.15 m and v = 8.0 m/s. Watch for: the energy bar growing to 160.0 J and 80.0 J, with the fraction still 0.333.
07

Where it matters

  • Rolling down a slope. With no slipping, the acceleration is g sin θ / (1 + c). A solid sphere (c = 2/5) gains speed fastest and a hoop (c = 1) slowest, whatever the masses and radii.
  • Wheels on vehicles. Part of the energy a car or bicycle gives its wheels goes into their spin. Wheels with their mass near the hub keep that share small.
  • Telling bodies apart. Two bodies with the same mass and radius can be told apart by how fast they roll down the same slope, which shows how their mass is spread.
08

Summary

In one line. A wheel rolls without sliding, and the sim follows how its kinetic energy is shared between moving forward and spinning.

Key points

  • Without sliding, v = ωr, so ω = v/r.
  • The top of the wheel moves at 2v, the centre at v, and the contact point is at rest for an instant.
  • KErot/KE = c/(1 + c), set by shape alone.

Common mix-ups

  • "The point touching the road moves fastest." It is at rest for that instant. The top of the wheel is fastest.
  • "Same speed means same energy split." The split depends on c, so shape matters even at equal v.
  • "A heavier wheel spins a larger share of its energy." Mass cancels out of the fraction.

Things to try on your own

  • Find the shape whose rotational fraction is 0.400, then check it against c = 2/3.
  • Predict ω for v = 6.0 m/s and r = 0.40 m, then read it from the panel.
  • Compare the pink part for the hoop and the disc at the same m, r and v.
